primitives.name: Functional Task Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: A functional analysis comprises the steps of (1) recognizing constraints that define the functional structure, (2) identifying sub-actions that subserve the achievement of structure-dependent goals, (3) explicating modalities as specifics of the movement execution, and (4) assigning functions to actions, sub-actions and modalities.
primitives.assumptions: Movement is goal-directed; sub-actions are modular and structure-dependent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When constraints are misidentified or sub-actions decouple from global goals.

The functional approach to movement analysis establishes a mathematical duality between task constraints and movement execution. It formalizes movement as a composition of sub-actions, each with a defined function in achieving a global goal. This leads to a structured decomposition where each component is evaluated for its contribution to the overall task. The breakdown regime occurs when sub-actions fail to maintain coherence with the global objective, resulting in functional inefficiency. From a GSI perspective, this translates into a Bayesian network where movement features are evidence variables conditioning on task goals. In GSE, it becomes a Markovian state transition system where each movement phase corresponds to a functional state. The dual nature of this framework allows for retroactive error tracing and predictive modeling of movement refinement strategies.
